newsitem.title: DENMARK: Sonofon buys new microwave GSM system.
newsitem.headline: Sonofon buys new microwave GSM system.

text.p: Danish telecoms operator Sonofon said on Thursday it placed a 60-70 million crown order for a new Mini Link microwave mobile telephone transmission system from Sweden's L.M. Ericsson.
It said the order covered equipment for some 700 transmission stations for completion by end-1999, with the first Mini Link transmitter going on line this August.
"The new microwave system means that a major part of Sonofon telephone calls will go through a 100 percent Sonofon-owned transmission network," Sonofon said in a statement.
The new system uses microwave transmission for mobile telephony, avoiding the need for the present link-up with fixed lines provided by Danish operator Tele Danmark, it said.
Sonofon, 53 percent owned by GN Store Nord, is the main competitor in Denmark of former monopoly operator Tele Danmark in mobile phones, with over 500,000 subscribers.
